newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report. [CORRECTED 20:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report. [CORRECTED 20:47 GMT]

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firm, recovering from their recent lows as the market steadied following selling tied to the Swiss franc's declines.
Short-term interest rates also recovered, with some respite offered by the dollar's move back below 1.28 francs in late trade after it hit highest levels against the franc in nearly two years.

Swiss traders saw as positive statements by U.S. deputy Treasury secretary Lawrence Summers that Washington would continue to strive for a balanced budget in President Clinton's second term in office.
But the Swiss Confederate bond yield remained high relative to where it has been earlier this year versus the Bund.
"The Bund has done very well versus the Conf. I think the spread will stay where it is," said one trader.
The Swiss 10-year yield spread has narrowed recently to roughly 195 basis points YLDS3 from roughly 210 where it had been in recent weeks.
The Swiss market lately has lost ground relative to German bonds as the Swiss franc drops on currency markets.
The Swiss franc's weakness has also pushed Swiss franc money rates higher.

In new issues, some Swiss syndicate managers were grumbling that latest deals have payment dates in 1997. Germany's DSL Bank issued a five-year 150 million Swiss franc bond with a 3-1/4 percent coupon quoted early yielding 3.29 percent by lead manager Credit Suisse CSST. Payment is January 21.

The issue was seen by one syndicate manager at another Swiss bank as meeting favourable demand. "It is a good yield. The deal is very well received, especially in the current environment," he said. But, he had a small complaint about the issue because of the payment date in January.
"An investor might prefer a more immediate payment date, so that they can begin receiving interest," he said.
Engadiner Kraftwerke AG announced a domestic 100 million Swiss franc issue with a 4-1/4 percent coupon for 12 years, with a call option at 10 and 11 years.
The issue, priced at 100.40 (corrects from 110.40), was quoted yielding 4.32 percent in late trade by lead manager SBC.
That issue has a payment date of January 10.
Syndicate managers said that there was talk that another energy firm may be considering a new issue as well.
